description: A complete Business Requirements Document generated exclusively from the provided ProjectKnowledge. ProjectKnowledge is the sole source of truth. Preserve the meaning and important details of the source knowledge while rewriting content into clear, concise, professional BRD language. Do not invent unsupported information, requirements, stakeholders, decisions, risks, assumptions, constraints, scope, metrics, technical details, or business facts. Preserve all meaningful qualifiers, actors, conditions, states, permissions, thresholds, values, units, dates, timing, limits, dependencies, and scope qualifiers. Every source requirement must remain represented in the appropriate BRD section.

executive_summary.description: A concise professional summary synthesized from ProjectKnowledge. It should explain what the project is, why it exists, its primary business goals, and its major scope or capability areas. It may synthesize information but must not introduce unsupported facts.

content.description: A concise but informative executive summary based only on ProjectKnowledge. Clearly communicate the project's purpose, primary business objectives, and major scope or capability areas. Improve clarity and readability without changing the meaning or adding unsupported information.

project_overview.description: Basic project information derived directly from ProjectKnowledge.

project_name.description: The project name from ProjectKnowledge. Preserve it faithfully and do not invent or rename the project.

description.description: A clear and concise description of the project based only on ProjectKnowledge. Preserve the project's purpose, primary capability, users, and important scope qualifiers when provided.

business_objectives.description: Business goals or intended business outcomes supported by ProjectKnowledge.

objectives.description: Business objectives supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve the original meaning and meaningful qualifiers. Do not convert functional capabilities into business objectives or invent new goals or metrics.

items.description: A complete business objective describing an intended business outcome. Preserve targets, metrics, business reasons, affected users, and other meaningful qualifiers when provided.

scope.description: The project's supported boundaries, including capabilities and activities that are in scope and items explicitly excluded or deferred.

in_scope.description: Capabilities, activities, workflows, or areas supported by ProjectKnowledge as part of the project scope. Derive these from explicit scope information and supported functional requirements. Do not invent capabilities and do not treat every unmentioned capability as out of scope.

items.description: A concrete item included within the project scope. Preserve important scope, release, phase, actor, or capability qualifiers.

out_of_scope.description: Features, capabilities, activities, users, integrations, phases, or areas explicitly excluded, deferred, or designated as outside the current project scope according to ProjectKnowledge. Do not infer exclusions from missing information.

items.description: An explicitly excluded or deferred scope item. Preserve any phase, release, timing, or other qualifier.

stakeholders.description: People, teams, organizations, or project roles identified as stakeholders in ProjectKnowledge.
All stakeholders supported by ProjectKnowledge. Do not add stakeholders based on typical project roles or external knowledge.

name.description: The stakeholder's name, role identifier, team, or organization name as provided by ProjectKnowledge.

role.description: The stakeholder's stated role or relationship to the project. Preserve null when no role is supported.

organization.description: The stakeholder's stated organization. Preserve null when no organization is supported.

business_requirements.description: High-level business needs derived from ProjectKnowledge. These may be synthesized from business objectives and related project knowledge but must remain directly supported by the source.

requirements.description: High-level business requirements describing what the business needs to achieve or what business capability is required. Do not introduce technical implementation details or unsupported business goals.

items.description: A clear, high-level business requirement. Express the business need or capability rather than implementation details. Preserve meaningful business context and qualifiers.

functional_requirements.description: Functional requirements derived from ProjectKnowledge. Every functional requirement from ProjectKnowledge must remain represented unless it is genuinely duplicated without loss of meaning.

requirements.description: All functional requirements supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve the meaning, actors, actions, objects, conditions, states, permissions, business rules, timing, limits, quantities, exceptions, and dependencies. Keep independently testable requirements separate.

items.description: A complete functional requirement written in clear professional BRD language. Preserve all meaningful qualifiers and do not add unsupported implementation details.

non_functional_requirements.description: Non-functional requirements derived from ProjectKnowledge. Every non-functional requirement must remain represented with its measurable values and meaningful qualifiers.

requirements.description: All non-functional requirements supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve security, performance, availability, reliability, scalability, usability, compliance, data integrity, and other quality requirements. Preserve all numeric values, thresholds, units, percentages, durations, frequencies, conditions, scope, actors, and qualifiers.

items.description: A complete non-functional requirement written in professional BRD language. Do not remove measurable values or contextual qualifiers. Do not reduce a requirement to only its category or numeric target.

assumptions_and_constraints.description: Assumptions and constraints supported by ProjectKnowledge. Keep the two concepts distinct.

assumptions.description: Assumptions explicitly supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve uncertainty and qualifiers. Do not convert assumptions into confirmed facts.

items.description: A project assumption preserved or clearly rewritten from ProjectKnowledge. Do not invent assumptions.

constraints.description: Constraints explicitly supported by ProjectKnowledge, including limitations, restrictions, dependencies, deadlines, mandated conditions, or resource limitations.

items.description: A project constraint preserving the affected area and meaningful limitations, thresholds, dependencies, deadlines, or conditions.

risks_and_decisions.description: Risks and confirmed decisions supported by ProjectKnowledge. Keep potential risks distinct from confirmed decisions.

risks.description: Risks explicitly supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve the potential issue, cause, consequence, uncertainty, affected area, and other meaningful context. Do not invent risks.

items.description: A project risk supported by ProjectKnowledge. Do not turn existing problems, assumptions, or open questions into risks unless the source identifies them as risks.

decisions.description: Confirmed project decisions supported by ProjectKnowledge. Do not convert suggestions, recommendations, possibilities, or unresolved alternatives into decisions.

items.description: A project decision preserving what was decided, its affected area, scope, conditions, rationale, or timing when supported by ProjectKnowledge.

open_questions.description: Questions, ambiguities, unresolved decisions, or missing information that remain open according to ProjectKnowledge.

questions.description: All open questions supported by ProjectKnowledge. Preserve the uncertainty and context. Do not answer them or convert them into requirements, assumptions, constraints, or decisions.

items.description: A clear representation of an unresolved project question or issue. Preserve the actual question and relevant context.
